name: MiniCLEAN
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

Status 'completed' rests on SNOLAB's own experiment page (status 'Completed'; 'began decommissioning in 2019'). The papers read (2014-2019) never report a liquid-argon physics run: 2014 expected cooling from summer 2014, 2017 papers report a cold-gas run (Feb-Apr 2017). A 2018 note about filling with natural argon (from the lead's brief) could not be verified and is not used.
Qualifies via 'approved and under construction' (assembly underway at SNOLAB in March 2014, arXiv:1403.4842); the approval date is not published in the sources read.
No dark matter search result was published by MiniCLEAN in the sources read; the only published result is a technology measurement (triplet lifetime in gaseous argon).
technology_class is 'other': MiniCLEAN is scintillation-only (single phase, no drift field), so the TPC classes would mislabel it; no noble-liquid scintillator class exists.

summary.plain: MiniCLEAN was a 500 kg detector of liquid argon (or liquid neon) in the Cube Hall at SNOLAB, Canada, built to test a simple single-phase way of hunting for WIMP dark matter. A cold-gas test run took place in 2017 and SNOLAB reports decommissioning began in 2019. No dark matter result was published.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid argon/neon scintillation detector: 92 cryogenic PMTs with nearly 4pi coverage of a 500 kg (150 kg fiducial) target in a stainless-steel inner vessel, inside a vacuum outer vessel and a water shield tank with a 48-PMT muon veto in the SNOLAB Cube Hall. Pulse-shape discrimination separates nuclear recoils from 39Ar beta events; a 39Ar spike was planned to demonstrate its reach. Prototype for a multi-tonne CLEAN detector. Only a cold-gas run (February-April 2017) is documented; it gave a triplet lifetime of 3.480 us in gaseous argon. No WIMP-search result is published.
